title: maple-crest-health-integration-call-notes-2026-08-12
content:
Attendees:
- Paul Green (Maple Crest IT)
- Ravi Shah (Integration lead, Maple Crest)
- Dr. Lena Ortiz (Compliance advisor, MC) - joined for first 15m
- Jordan Lee (Redwood SE)
- Maya Thompson (Redwood, notes)

High-level summary:
- Initial integration scoping call for Redwood Private (VPC) deployment to serve patient-facing triage chat and clinical documentation summarization.
- Customer requirement: on-prem/persistent VPC deployment with no PHI leaving their environment; must support audit logs and KMS integration.
- Target: pilot with 3 clinics by end of Q4 2026, scale to 50 clinics in 2027.

Key requirements (explicit):
- Data residency: all inference inside customer VPC, no telemetry to Redwood hosted control-plane without explicit opt-in.
- KMS/HSM: integrate with customer AWS KMS CMKs for model decryption and secrets.
- SSO & RBAC: SAML SSO for console access, role-based access at team and clinic level.
- Audit logs: detailed per-request logs retained 1 year (they may request 7 years pending legal).
- Latency: median latency target <= 150ms per token for short prompts (~256 tokens).
- Throughput: initial expected peak 30 rps across 3 clinics, burst to 200 rps in high-concurrency periods.
- Model: start with open LLM (Redwood-recommended 13B quantized variant), can consider customer-provided model later.

Technical constraints / gotchas mentioned:
- Existing network setup: customer runs in a restricted subnet with egress blocked. We need the deployment appliance to be able to pull images/builds initially or they will provide air-gapped bundles.
- Regulatory: Dr. Ortiz flagged potential need for BAA and SOC2 + additional regional attestation; legal to follow up.
- Storage: persistent KV/cache must be encrypted at rest and use their CMK. They currently use S3 with server-side encryption but want explicit KMS usage rather than Redwood-managed keys.
- Firewall: they will provide a list of outbound endpoints allowed. Must confirm control-plane callback URLs if any are needed for telemetry/heartbeat. They prefer a control-plane-only topology where the control-plane sits in a Red Hat OpenShift cluster inside their cloud rather than contacting a Redwood-managed public control-plane.
- Secrets handling: customer wants proof that keys never leave HSM boundary; need to describe Redwood Private installer KMS integration flow and where customer keys are used.
- Telemetry: by default Redwood runtime collects lite metrics for autoscaling; customer requires per-request opt-in and a mode that emits only anonymized metrics or none.

Deployment & infra notes:
- Suggested topology: customer-managed control-plane in their VPC -> Redwood Private runtime nodes in private subnets -> model artifacts pulled from an S3 bucket encrypted with their CMK or loaded via air-gapped bundle.
- Image delivery: two options discussed: (1) initial bootstrap uses temporary egress and image pull from Redwood registry, afterwards egress blocked; (2) customer requests air-gapped tarball + installer. They lean toward option 2 for security.
- Ports/endpoints: need to confirm required outbound endpoints. Action: Jordan to send minimal whitelist list by 2026-08-14.
- KMS flow: require step-by-step diagram showing where CMK decrypt occurs. Action: SE to prepare and share by 2026-08-18.

Pilot plan (timeline):
- Week 1 (Aug 17-23): provide install checklist + pre-reqs, gather network contacts and SOC contacts.
- Week 2 (Aug 24-30): customer prepares air-gap bundle OR grants temporary egress; SE tests bootstrap in staging.
- Week 3 (Sept 1-7): deploy runtime to 1 clinic environment, run canary traffic with synthetic prompts.
- Week 4-6 (Sept 8-28): iterate on latency tuning, RBAC config, audit log verification.
- October: expand to remaining 2 pilot clinics, finalize runbook and handoff to ops.

Open questions / risks:
- Legal: BAA and retention requirements (1 year vs 7 years) could change architecture (longer retention requires storage/PII workflow).
- Throughput scaling: customer peak bursts to 200 rps may require Dedicated-style reserved GPU pools; need cost estimate.
- Model verification: can the recommended 13B quantized variant meet their clinical accuracy needs? They want a short eval run on 500 real-world triage prompts.
- Failover: if customer control-plane becomes isolated, runtime must continue serving from cached model + local health checks; need to validate offline behavior and license checks.

Action items (owner - due):
- Jordan Lee (SE) - send minimal outbound whitelist and ports; 2026-08-14.
- Jordan Lee (SE) - prepare KMS/HSM sequence diagram and installer flow for air-gapped install; 2026-08-18.
- Maya Thompson - draft pilot SOW and cost ballpark for Dedicated vs Private for 200 rps burst; 2026-08-20.
- Paul Green (MC) - confirm legal contacts and who will lead BAA review; 2026-08-16.
- Ravi Shah (MC) - provide sample triage prompts and representative docs for 500-eval set; 2026-08-21.

Notes for follow-up meeting (suggested agenda):
- Walkthrough of KMS/HSM flow and installer artifacts (20m)
- Review pilot SOW and cost scenarios (15m)
- Discuss telemetry/opt-in modes and auditing (15m)
- Next steps on legal/BAA timeline (10m)

Attachments / refs:
- Confluence MC-Integrations-1832 (integration spec)
- Jira ENG-4721 (installer work)
- Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/connectors/maple-crest/pull/12

Misc notes / personal scratchpad items:
- Might recommend building a lightweight gateway in front of runtime for clinics to reduce concurrent connections.
- Consider proposing LRU cache sizing guidance for KV cache based on 30 rps baseline.
- If they insist on 7yr logs, need to discuss cold storage and retrieval costs.

Next meeting: propose 2026-08-19 for technical deep-dive (Jordan + Ravi + Maya + Paul).

Recorded by: Maya Thompson, Redwood Inference (solutions-engineering)
